title: Open model entry spec and rollback scenarios for minor releases
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Clarify the requirements and acceptance criteria for onboarding new open (community) model variants into the catalog, with a focus on how we treat minor releases (semver minor/patch), the required compatibility metadata (compatibility signatures / runtime capability flags), and a deterministic rollback/degradation policy that can be automated by the platform.

Background: We continue to admit community weights frequently. Historically we either pin a specific checkpoint (hard pin) or accept unpinned community variants which introduces runtime surprises. Product needs a lightweight, operator-friendly intake that balances developer velocity with runtime safety and predictable user experience. This ticket defines a stepwise onboarding flow and the set of metadata and runtime behaviors required for minor releases and patch variants.

Core concepts introduced in this spec (unique phrasing):
- Compatibility signature: a compact, machine-readable string attached to a catalog entry that indexes declared runtime capabilities (kv_cache_compatible, fp16_ok, attention_type:flash|triton, max_token_context). The signature must be present for any model with a variant label "open-community".
- Soft-pin signal: a non-blocking hint stored in the catalog and propagated to routing that biases serving to prefer a pinned checkpoint for a configurable warmup window (default 48h) without preventing fallback. Soft-pins decay automatically and are superseded by hard-pins.
- Degradation policy: a short, actionable policy that enumerates the automatic fallback chain and rollback triggers (quality delta, latency SLO breach, memory OOMs). The policy is evaluated by the runtime and the catalog control plane during rollouts.

Requirements (functional):
1) Intake metadata: Every new open model entry must provide: human_name, model_checkpoint_uri, semver, compatibility_signature (see schema below), minimum_supported_runtime_version, resource_profile_hint (gpu_type, vram_est), and an explicit pin_intent: [soft|hard|unpin].
2) Compatibility signature schema: simple CSV of capability tokens with optional numeric kv pairs. Example: "kv=1;fp16=true;attn=flash;ctx=8192". Platform must validate tokens against the accepted capability set and surface validation errors in the intake UI.
3) Soft-pin behavior: When a pin_intent=soft is set during intake, the control plane stores pin_age and routes new traffic to the checkpoint with decreasing bias over the warmup window. The runtime must still allow fallback to previous pinned variants when capacity or compatibility mismatch occurs.
4) Minor-release policy: For semver increases where major == same and minor > previous minor, the model is eligible for a staged rollout (canary -> ramp). Default canary = 5% for 4 hours, ramp = linear to 50% over 6 hours, then to 100% manual approval. The control plane must support configuring these parameters per-entry.
5) Rollback triggers & automated rollback: runtime/monitoring pipeline must evaluate: (a) eval-set quality drop > 3% absolute or >7% relative, (b) 95th percentile latency increase > 20% vs baseline for 15min, (c) error-rate spike > 1% absolute. Any of these should mark the rollout as unstable; the control plane must (by default) automatically revert traffic to the prior pinned variant and create a rollback incident with links to logs/metrics.
6) Observability: New catalog entries must create dashboard templates: rollout_health, latency_by_route, quality_regressions_by_promptset. Rollout change events must produce structured audit logs for compliance.
7) E2E tests & CI: Add a lightweight CI job that validates compatibility_signature parsing, soft-pin routing bias under simulated capacity constraints, canary ramping logic, and automated rollback action (mock).

Non-functional requirements:
- Backward compatibility: Existing pinned variants behavior must be unchanged by default. Soft-pin is opt-in and must not impact existing hard-pin semantics.
- Performance: Adding compatibility_signature checks to intake must not add more than 200ms to UI save latency.
- Failure modes: If compatibility_signature is missing for a model marked as open-community, intake fails. If runtime encounters unknown capability tokens at serving time, it should treat them as conservative (assume incompatible) and fall back to compatible variant.

Acceptance criteria (flattened list provided below): see acceptance_criteria field for discrete items.

Outcomes & success metrics:
- Reduce emergency rollback incidents for community models by 60% in the first quarter after launch (tracked via incident dashboard).
- Time-to-onboard (operator completing intake) average <= 10 minutes for compliant entries.
- Percent of minor releases that complete automated ramp without rollback >= 85% within 30 days of rollout.

Implementation notes for Eng: Runtime must expose an API hook: GET /catalog/compat/{signature} -> normalized capability set and a predicate function (string). Routing layer must accept a soft_pin_weight parameter and expose it to the traffic-steering heuristics. Catalog UI must validate signature tokens client-side and back-end re-validate server-side.

Acceptance test data: provide two synthetic community model entries: "synth-small:v1.4.2" with compatibility_signature "kv=1;fp16=true;attn=triton;ctx=4096" and "synth-large:v2.0.1" with compatibility_signature "kv=0;fp16=false;attn=flash;ctx=8192" for QA to exercise fallback and signature validation.

Links to artifacts: included in links field.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to the behavior for minor/patch releases and the metadata required at intake. Major-release policy (breaking changes) is covered in a separate PRD.

Stakeholders: PM (Ava), Eng (Luca, Priya Reddy), Runtime lead (Diego Alvarez), DX/Console (Mei Chen), Security/Compliance (Jamal Reed)
acceptance_criteria: Catalog intake UI enforces presence and syntactic validation of compatibility_signature for open-community entries.
Soft-pin toggle exposed in the intake form with a configurable warmup window (default 48h).
Routing honors soft-pin biasing during canary/ramp and allows fallback to prior pinned variants under capacity or compatibility mismatch.
Minor-release default rollout policy created and controllable per-entry (5% canary, linear ramp to 50% over 6h) with ability to abort to 0% and revert to previous variant.
Automated rollback triggers implemented and tested for eval-quality drops, latency SLO breaches, and error spikes (see thresholds in spec).
Dashboard templates for rollout health and quality regressions provisioned automatically for new entries and linked from the catalog entry page.
CI job added that validates signature parsing, soft-pin routing behavior (simulated), and automated rollback action (mocked).
Documentation (catalog intake guide + operator runbook) published and linked from the intake flow.
Audit logs contain structured rollout events and rollback reasons for compliance review.
E2E smoke test using synthetic entries passes in staging: canary ramp, simulated quality regression causes auto-revert, and soft-pin decays after warmup window.
out_of_scope: Major release compatibility gating (breaking API surface changes).
On-prem installation bundling changes; private deployment nuances are tracked separately.
Deep model validation (we only validate declared capability tokens, not full model correctness).
